'''Gerald Marron Scherba''' (February 9, 1927 – February 5, 2001) was an American [[biologist]].

== Life and career ==
Scherba was born in [[Chicago, Illinois]], the son of Harry Scherba. He attended the [[University of Chicago]], earning his [[Bachelor of Science|BS degree]] in [[biology]] in 1950, his [[Master of Science|MS degree]] in 1952 and his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in 1955.<ref name="a">{{Cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/The_Coyote_Chronicles/x581r0jXQ2QC?hl=en&gbpv=0|title=The Coyote Chronicles: A Chronological History of California State University, San Bernardino, 1960-2010|page=171|first=Michael|last=Burgess|publisher=Wildside Press, LLC|date=July 2010|ISBN=9781434411570|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

Scherba served as an [[associate professor]] in the department of biology at [[California State University, Chico]] from 1955 to 1962. He then served as a professor in the department of [[natural science]]s at [[California State University, San Bernardino]] from 1962 to 1984.<ref name="a" /> During his years as a professor, in 1963, he was named a [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science|fellow]] of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic?field_last_name_value=All&field_address_city=All&field_address_when_elected_administrative_area=All&field_address_when_elected_country_code=All&field_year_elected=&field_primary_aaas_section=All&field_status_value=All&field_year_status_changed_value=&name_combine=scherba&field_institutional_affiliation_value=|title=Historic Fellows|work=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref>

== Death ==
Scherba died of [[Heart failure|congestive heart failure]] on February 5, 2001, at the age of 73.<ref name="a" />
